title: Add persistent config to your CLI tool
description: Give a real CLI tool an OS-conventional state location, a documented config format and precedence order, a properly stored credential, and a migration path for anyone already using an earlier version.

learningObjectives.text: Implement OS-conventional locations for a tool's config, cache and data
Store a credential with a keychain-first, explicitly-announced fallback strategy

contentSections.title: The lab

contentSections.body: Every filter from this module — where state lives, which format fits, what order sources resolve in, when an env var beats a file, how a credential is actually stored, how a migration protects the original — is easiest to get right by building it once, deliberately, on a real tool. This lab adds real, working config handling to a CLI tool of your own (invtrack if you've been following along, your tool from the tool-ideas phase, or a new small one built for this lab).

contentSections.title: Persistent config for your CLI tool
contentSections.brief: Pick a CLI tool that needs at least one persistent setting and one credential — reuse a tool from an earlier module if you have one, or build a small one now (a tool that posts to a webhook needs a URL and a token; a backup checker needs a source path and cloud credentials). You'll give it real state directories, a real config file with real precedence, a properly stored credential, and a migration path for an imagined earlier version.
contentSections.deliverable: A tool that reads and writes config safely, with a credential stored properly

stages.title: Set up the state directories
stages.instructions: Use env-paths (or write the per-OS logic by hand if you'd rather) to get real config, cache and data directories for your tool. Write down which of your tool's actual values goes in which directory, and why each one belongs there rather than another.
stages.checkpoint: Config, cache and data each resolve to a real, OS-conventional path, and you can name why each value you store belongs in the directory you chose.

stages.title: Build the config file and precedence
stages.instructions: Choose a format (justify it against lesson 2's criteria), write a real config file, and implement resolution across at least three sources — a CLI flag, an environment variable, and the file — in one documented, fixed order. Add a way to see which source won for each value (a --show-config flag or equivalent).
stages.checkpoint: At least one setting can be set via flag, env var, and file, resolves in the documented order, and its resolved source is visible to the user.

stages.title: Store the credential properly
stages.instructions: Store your tool's credential using a keychain-first strategy with an explicit, announced fallback (env var, then a permission-restricted file) for when the keychain isn't available. Implement a masking function and confirm the full credential never appears in a printed value or a --verbose-equivalent log.
stages.checkpoint: The credential is never printed or logged in full anywhere in the tool, and the fallback path (when the keychain is unavailable) is explicit and announced, not silent.

stages.title: Write the migration path
stages.instructions: Add an explicit version field to your config file's shape. Write a loader that detects an older (or hypothetical earlier) version, migrates it in memory, backs up the original file before writing the migrated one, and announces the migration once on stderr.
stages.checkpoint: The config loader detects an old version by its version field, backs up the original before overwriting, and prints a one-line migration notice to stderr.

rubric.criterion: State locations are OS-conventional, not cwd-relative
rubric.meets: Config, cache and data each resolve via env-paths (or equivalent) to a fixed home-directory location, never process.cwd().

rubric.criterion: Config format matches who edits the file
rubric.meets: The chosen format is justified against whether the file needs comments, nesting, or neither — not picked by default.

rubric.criterion: Precedence is fixed, documented, and visible
rubric.meets: At least one value resolves across flag, env var and file in a stated order, and the user can see which source won.

rubric.criterion: The credential is never exposed in full
rubric.meets: No code path prints or logs the full credential; a masked form is used wherever a value needs to be shown.

rubric.criterion: The keychain fallback is explicit, not silent
rubric.meets: When the keychain is unavailable, the tool falls back to env var then file and announces the fallback once on stderr.

rubric.criterion: The migration protects the original file
rubric.meets: A backup of the pre-migration file exists on disk before the migrated version is written, and the migration is announced once.

contentSections.body: Config and secrets handling is invisible when it's right and a support thread when it's wrong — this lab is where it gets built right the first time, not patched after a bug report.

title: Checkpoint — State, Config and Secrets
description: Ten questions: four from this module, four from Designing a CLI People Won't Fight, two from further back in the tool-ideas phase. Ungraded, untimed.

contentSections.title: Let's see what stuck
